macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rebounds modestly after AI-led sell-off
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.3% and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% Friday, while the Dow slipped 0.5%, as technology shares recovered part of their steep weekly losses.[2]

items.title: Strong U.S. jobs report reshapes rate outlook
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above forecasts of about 65,000, while unemployment fell to 4.1%. The stronger labor market kept Treasury yields firm and complicated expectations for future Federal Reserve policy.[2]

items.title: AI infrastructure stocks remain under pressure
items.summary: Investors continued to reassess the outlook for AI-related capital spending and data-center development after the U.S. midterm elections, contributing to major volatility and a sharp weekly decline in technology shares.[6]

items.title: Inflation data and Fed appearances ahead
items.summary: U.S. markets are preparing for October CPI and PPI reports, along with speeches by Federal Reserve officials, making inflation and monetary policy the key macroeconomic focus for the coming week.[1]

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway reports lower operating earnings
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway reported third-quarter operating earnings of $12.7 billion, down about 6% year over year and roughly in line with estimates, while its shares had been among the week’s stronger large-cap financial performers.[8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: U.S. Treasury cuts MEXC Global off from financial system
items.summary: FinCEN issued an order prohibiting U.S. financial institutions from transferring funds with MEXC Global, citing alleged facilitation of more than $16 billion in transactions connected to sanctions evasion and cybercrime.[1]

items.title: Bitcoin remains below $76,000 as crypto pressure persists
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $75,777, little changed over 24 hours, while Ether, XRP, Solana, Cardano and Dogecoin posted modest declines.[3]

items.title: Binance prepares to close certain European customer accounts
items.summary: Binance plans to close affected accounts in France, Spain, Italy and Poland by December 31 after the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets transition period ends; remaining balances may incur a monthly fee beginning November 29.[3]

items.title: Ethereum testnet upgrade delayed amid gas-accounting concerns
items.summary: Developers postponed the Hoodi testnet upgrade to address risks associated with EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, while spot Ethereum ETFs recorded roughly $365 million in weekly outflows.[2]

items.title: Circle mints $250 million in USDC on Solana
items.summary: Circle’s USDC Treasury minted approximately 250 million USDC on the Solana network, according to on-chain monitoring.[1]

items.title: Fidelity transfers approximately 27,000 ETH to Galaxy Digital
items.summary: On-chain monitoring identified a transfer of roughly 27,000 ETH, valued at about $60 million, from Fidelity to Galaxy Digital.[1]

items.title: China halts planned Solana event and investigates local entities
items.summary: Chinese authorities reportedly stopped a planned Solana Accelerate China 2026 gathering and investigated local entities after classifying Solana-related advertising as virtual-currency marketing.[5]

items.title: Algorand pauses plan to remove ALGO supply cap
items.summary: The Algorand Foundation indefinitely paused Project King Safety, which would have removed the ALGO token’s supply cap, while extending staking rewards through January 2028.[2]

items.title: Taurus adds smart-contract asset support on Stellar
items.summary: Digital-asset infrastructure provider Taurus launched live smart-contract asset support on Stellar, enabling institutions to custody, issue and manage programmable assets with approval and governance controls.[4]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI previews GPT-Red for automated model flaw discovery
items.summary: OpenAI previewed GPT-Red, a self-play system designed to find vulnerabilities in AI models. The system reportedly identified prompt-injection weaknesses in GPT-5.1 at a rate 6.5 times higher than human red-teamers.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 across ChatGPT, Codex and API
items.summary: OpenAI began rolling out the GPT-5.6 model family across its consumer, coding and developer products, claiming improved speed, cost efficiency and agentic-task performance.

items.title: Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs unveil biosecurity framework
items.summary: The organizations announced a framework intended to control access to biological AI capabilities, combining pathogen-sequencing tools with DNA watermarking and safety gates.

items.title: Anthropic offers premium Claude access to U.S. K-12 teachers
items.summary: Anthropic announced a Claude for Teachers initiative providing premium-model access and classroom integrations, beginning with a pilot in Detroit public schools.

items.title: Meta opens Muse Spark 1.1 API preview
items.summary: Meta made its Muse Spark 1.1 agentic coding model available to developers through a public API preview. The model reportedly supports a one-million-token context window.

items.title: AI data-center opposition emerges as infrastructure constraint
items.summary: JPMorgan warned that growing public and political opposition to data centers could lengthen negotiations, increase costs and delay AI infrastructure projects, even as construction capacity continues to expand.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly closes initial $11 billion funding tranche
items.summary: A financial-industry roundup reported that OpenAI had closed an initial tranche of approximately $11 billion at a valuation of about $1.25 trillion, with the broader financing round still pending.

items.title: AI safety office faces independence concerns
items.summary: The Associated Press reported that staff at a U.S. Commerce Department AI-safety division had been asked to informally report to the White House while the office lacked a permanent leader and had stopped publishing research.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonuses tied to story progression
items.summary: Rockstar’s official information indicates that some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonuses will be unlocked progressively rather than being available at launch, suggesting a chapter-based structure for the game’s campaign.

items.title: GTA 6 preorder revenue reportedly reaches $751 million
items.summary: Sensor Tower data cited in reporting estimates 7.71 million GTA 6 preorders and approximately $751 million in revenue ahead of the reported November 19 release. Most purchases were reportedly for the $100 Ultimate Edition.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches
items.summary: A highly anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time reportedly launched this week after years of speculation about a revival of the classic Nintendo title.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls VI reportedly confirmed as Sentinel, set in Hammerfell
items.summary: Bethesda reportedly revealed the title The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel and confirmed Hammerfell as the game’s setting, though few additional details were disclosed.

items.title: Microsoft rolls out redesigned Xbox PC app to Insiders
items.summary: Microsoft is testing a redesigned Xbox app for PC, claiming launch times up to 60% faster and loading times up to 50% faster for key pages.

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly bids for Arkane Studios
items.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly among several parties seeking to acquire Arkane Studios from Microsoft, while Arkane management may also be considering an independent buyout.

items.title: Path of Exile 2 to leave early access and become free-to-play
items.summary: Path of Exile 2 is reportedly scheduled to leave early access and transition to a free-to-play model on December 11.

items.title: Valve antitrust arbitrations face potential closure
items.summary: A federal judge in Seattle declined to issue a preliminary injunction that would have prevented the closure of nearly 15,000 gamers’ antitrust arbitrations against Valve.
